A home guard on deputation to the Railway Protection Force (RPF) was arrested after visuals of him beating a woman and dragging her by her hair across the street went viral on social media. The incident took place on the evening of Friday, September 18, outside Hyderabad’s Hafeezpet Railway station. The home guard, Anand, has also been dismissed from service. In the FIR registered against Anand at Miyapur police station, the complainant, head constable S Gopal, stated that he got to know about the assault while he was out on patrol. Gopal was accompanied by Special Police Officer (SPO) Rajeshwar Reddy. Gopal said in his complaint that they made enquiries after learning about the assault and came to know that Anand was involved. However, they were unable to trace the woman who was allegedly assaulted. The case against Anand was registered under Sections 74 (punishes assault or the use of criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty) and 118(1) (voluntarily causing bodily hurt using dangerous weapons or hazardous means) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). items.title: Tulu is now an additional official language in Karnataka
items.summary: Karnataka’s Cabinet has approved Tulu as an additional language for administrative purposes in Dakshina Kannada and Udupi. The move will allow government offices in the two districts to use Tulu for administrative work, with the government allocating Rs 82 lakh annually for translation, training and related activities. The decision comes after years of demands from Tulu organisations for greater recognition, including inclusion in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution. The move also comes against the backdrop of Tulu’s cultural and political significance in coastal Karnataka. Pro-Kannada organisations, including Karnataka Rakshana Vedike, have also supported the recognition of Tulu while calling for the development of both languages.
